CVE-2024-24576.f010dcb6af48234021de16ac2fde9ffd55642ec4:
osproc: refuse cmd.exe metacharacters in arguments to .bat/.cmd files on Windows (#26584)

On Windows, `CreateProcess` runs `.bat`/`.cmd` files through `cmd.exe
/c`. cmd.exe parses the command line again with its own rules, so
`startProcess("tool.bat", args = [x])` lets `x` inject commands:
`a&calc` passes `quoteShellWindows` unquoted, `%VAR%` expands even
inside quotes, and an embedded `\"` breaks cmd.exe's quote pairing. This
is the "BatBadBut" class (CVE-2024-24576).

The fix fails closed, the same way Rust 1.77.2 does for arguments it
can't escape:
- If `command` is a `.bat`/`.cmd` file (case-insensitive, trailing dots
and spaces ignored as Windows does) and `poEvalCommand` isn't set,
`startProcess` raises `OSError` when any argument contains `& | < > ^ %
! "` or a line break.
- The check runs before any pipe handles are created, so nothing leaks.
- `OSError` keeps the `raises: [OSError, IOError]` contract unchanged.
- `.exe` targets and `poEvalCommand` behave exactly as before. A name
without an extension can't resolve to a batch file, because
`CreateProcess` only appends `.exe`.

The PR also documents this on `startProcess`, adds a changelog entry,
and adds a Windows-only test in `tests/stdlib/tosproc.nim`.

GHSA-4XC7-FP2P-49J3.59850c2034019651170df9a36f52c25082975a62:
httpclient: reject CR/LF in the request target and headers (STD-006)

The fix for GHSA-4xc7-fp2p-49j3 only checks string URLs for newlines.
A `Uri` whose path, query or hostname contains CR/LF, as well as header
names and values (per-request or `client.headers`), were written into
the request unchanged, allowing header and request injection.

`generateHeaders` now raises `ValueError` for CR, LF or NUL in the
request target, the Host header parts and every header field, before
anything is sent.

CVE-2021-29922.0d3af5454b66dfe4a8a7017030708a890207c658:
Only allow IPv4 literals in strict form (#18656)

* Only allow IPv4 literals in strict form

The strict form as defined in RFC 6943, section 3.1.1 only allows the dotted
form ddd.ddd.ddd.ddd of IPv4 literals, where ddd is a one to three digit decimal
number between 0 and 255. Until now octal numbers (with a leading zero) were
interpreted as decimal numbers which has security implications, see
CVE-2021-29922 and CVE-2021-29923.

* Update lib/pure/net.nim

Co-authored-by: Dominik Picheta <dominikpicheta@googlemail.com>
